title: Docking Layout Persistence

oracle.positive: Persist dock positions and reopen same named panel IDs
oracle.negative: Removed/unrecognized panel ID ignored with warning not crash

reviewer.role: project owner (human reviewer) running the app on Windows

checks_run: RED: cargo test -p om9-app --test dock_layout_persistence -> 4 passed; 2 failed (the store wrote nothing because a model-side change never marked the session dirty; and five repairs in normalize had no diagnostic)
GREEN: cargo test -p om9-app --test dock_layout_persistence -> 6 passed; 0 failed (S1..S4 positive, M1..M13 negative)
cargo test -p om9-app --lib: 83 passed; cargo test --workspace: every group ok; cargo check --workspace --all-targets: exit 0
cargo fmt --check: exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0
real windows: L3-002 size matrix 14/14 PASS; L3-003 panel scenarios 7/7 PASS (normalize runs on every load, so both harnesses re-ran)
code_change: dock_layout.rs::normalize now reports every repair it makes: a panel size outside its bounds, a menu height outside its bounds, a floating rectangle that is not finite, a floating rectangle below the minimum, and menu orders that were not dense. Its own contract is 'Diagnostics are user-visible warnings, never silent data loss', and the L3 negative oracle asks for an ignored id to be reported with a warning.
dense_section_orders now returns whether it changed anything, so the renumbering is reported instead of silent.
No behaviour change to what is stored or restored: the same keys, the same values, the same schema.

manual_reviewer_checklist.scope_note: The unit tests write and read real files; only the owner can confirm the session behaviour of the shipped application.

items.step: Arrange the menus (dock one right, roll one up, reorder, float one, hide one, resize the rail), run View ▸ Matrix Menus ▸ Set as Default, close the app, start it again.
items.machine_proven: S1/S2/S3: the written file reopens byte for byte, with the same named ids, orders, roll-up states, floating rectangle, height, rail width and right column.
items.human_must_verify: The window opens exactly as you left it: same order, same sizes, the floating menu back in the same place, the hidden menu still hidden.

items.step: Arrange the menus, change them again without running Set as Default, then Reload Menus. Repeat with Set as Default in between.
items.machine_proven: the store is the only writer; reload without a kept file is the documented baseline (S4).
items.human_must_verify: Reload brings back the kept configuration; changes you did not keep are discarded; the status line says which of the two happened.

items.step: Put a layout file that names a panel the program no longer has (for example key right-dock.project-manager) at the layout path and start the app.
items.machine_proven: M1/M2: an unknown panel or menu id is removed with the warning "... is not recognized; removed", and the rest of the file still loads.
items.human_must_verify: The app starts, the finished arrangement is kept for every name it still knows, and the status/history names the id it dropped.

items.step: Put a layout file with an absurd value in it (rail width 5000, a zero-sized floating rectangle, two menus with the same order) at the layout path and start the app.
items.machine_proven: M4/M5/M8: each repair is clamped or renumbered and reported with a warning; nothing is silently changed.
items.human_must_verify: The app starts with a usable arrangement and the status/history lists what it repaired.

items.step: Make the layout file unreadable (garbage bytes, or delete it) and start the app.
items.machine_proven: M10/M11/M12: unreadable, empty and oversized files are refused; a missing file is a clean baseline with no warning (S4).
items.human_must_verify: The app always starts: garbage is reported and ignored, a missing file is silent, and no menu is lost.
